d4cf4c21f55e46e51d1a9997686172e27df5c35c: A resort on a human scale, Altaussee – Loser focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 34 km of runs are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who don't need to keep changing their playground. The family reputation of Altaussee – Loser is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The moderate altitude of Altaussee – Loser, starting at 850 m and topping out at 1,800 m, makes it sensitive to climatic variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before departure is strongly recommended. The budget for a stay in Altaussee – Loser is clearly high: the day lift pass costs 59€, on top of accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before setting off. In short, Altaussee – Loser does not compete with the ski giants, nor does it claim to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
